title: Everyday masoor dal tadka
summary: The default weeknight dal. Red lentils need no soaking and no pressure cooker - twenty minutes in an open pan and they collapse on their own.

ingredients.qty: 1 cup (200 g), rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.note: The tadka fat. Ghee tastes best; any oil works.
Stir in for the last 3 minutes if you want dal palak.

steps: Put the rinsed dal, water, turmeric and half the salt in a pan. Bring to a boil, then drop to a simmer.
Skim off the grey foam that rises in the first few minutes - it makes the dal taste cleaner.
Simmer uncovered 18-22 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely lost their shape. Add hot water if it thickens past the consistency you want.
Meanwhile make the tadka: heat the ghee in a small pan, crackle the cumin, then the garlic. Take it to properly golden - this is where the flavour is.
Add asafoetida, onion and chilli, cook 3 minutes, then the tomato and chilli powder. Cook until the tomato breaks down, about 3 minutes more.
Pour the tadka into the dal - it will hiss. Stir, add the rest of the salt, simmer together 2 minutes.
Off the heat: lemon and coriander. Do not skip the lemon, it is what makes it taste finished.
tips: Salt at the start is fine for masoor. For chana or rajma, salt at the end or the skins toughen.
In a pressure cooker: dal, water and turmeric for 2 whistles, then pour the tadka in after.
It thickens a lot in the fridge. Loosen with hot water when reheating, not cold.
health_notes: About 10 g of fibre a serving and a genuinely cheap protein. Make it vegan by using oil instead of ghee - it loses a little depth, nothing more.

source.adapted: Standard home dal, with the tadka cut to one tablespoon of fat.
